stem: 10. A 25-year-old woman presents with eye pain, tearing, and photophobia. She has a history of contact lens use. Fluorescein staining shows a corneal ulcer. What is she at risk for?
explanation_verbatim: A corneal ulcer, especially in contact lens users, can progress to perforation if untreated. This may lead to endophthalmitis and vision loss.

11. A young boy with Down syndrome presents to the ophthalmologist with conical protrusion and thinning of the cornea. Which of the following is a useful tool for decision making and management of that patient?
explanation_verbatim: Investigations of keratoconus → Corneal topography (Map of corneal curvature is diagnostic), Pachymetry (measurement of the corneal thickness) & Pentacam (It gives, in addition to both topography and corneal thickness data, other data that help decision making and management of KC).

stem: 12. Which of the following is used to detect corneal abrasions?
12. Which of the following is used to detect corneal abrasions?
explanation_verbatim: Corneal epithelial defects (e.g. abrasions) are demonstrated by staining with 1% fluorescein sodium and viewing with cobalt blue filtered light.

stem: 13. Which of the following is among the side effects that accompany the use of local anaesthetics?
13. Which of the following is among the side effects that accompany the use of local anaesthetics?
explanation_verbatim: Local anesthetics cause corneal epithelial defects; this is why they are not advised during the treatment of photokeratitis (as they delay the healing process by causing corneal epithelial defects)

stem: 14. What is the initial management in case of chemical eye burn?
14. What is the initial management in case of chemical eye burn?
explanation_verbatim: The initial management of a case presenting with an intra-ocular foreign body is copious irrigation. However, the definitive management of that case is surgical removal of the foreign body.

stem: 15. What is the grade of chemical eye injury that is characterized by total loss of corneal epithelium and stromal haze obscuring iris details?
15. What is the grade of chemical eye injury that is characterized by total loss of corneal epithelium and stromal haze obscuring iris details?
explanation_verbatim:
Grading of chemical eye injuries →
A. Grade 1: (excellent prognosis): Clear cornea (epithelial damage only) and no limbal ischaemia.
B. Grade 2: (good prognosis): Hazy cornea but with visible iris detail and less than 30% limbal ischaemia.
C. Grade 3: (guarded prognosis):
● Total loss of corneal epithelium.
● Stromal haze obscuring iris detail.
1/3 to 1/2 limbal ischaemia.
D. Grade 4: (poor prognosis):
● Opaque cornea.
● More than 50% limbal ischaemia.

stem: 16. A patient with iridocyclitis was found to have WBC clumps on the back surface of the cornea. Which of the following might occur as a complication of that condition?
16. A patient with iridocyclitis was found to have WBC clumps on the back surface of the cornea. Which of the following might occur as a complication of that condition?
explanation_verbatim: Anterior uveitis can be complicated by 2ry glaucoma, Posterior synechiae, Complicated cataract, Calcific band keratopathy (if the iritis becomes chronic) especially in juvenile idiopathic arthritis & Macular oedema (if the iritis becomes chronic).
